key_features: An irregular, asymmetric light-brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with an off-center pink, structureless area with fine vessels (possible regression) and uneven pigment at the edge, a pattern that raises concern for early melanoma.

Symmetric oval tan-brown lesion with a regular, uniform rim of peripheral brown globules (a growing-nevus pattern), homogeneous center and only subtle central pinkish-gray area, with no atypical network, streaks or blue-white veil.
Irregular, asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (brown, blue-gray, pink), regression-like whitish areas, atypical network, peppering/gray granules and irregular pigmentation at the periphery.

Large asymmetric lesion with very dark brown-black pigmentation, irregular radial streaks/pseudopods at the periphery, blue-white veil areas centrally, and an eccentric light-brown asymmetric extension.
Facial-type chronically sun-damaged skin with asymmetric pigmented follicular openings, annular-granular and rhomboidal brown structures, and a focal blue-gray area, suggesting lentigo maligna.

Asymmetric pigmentation with eccentric dark red-brown blotches, central structureless pinkish hypopigmented area, and an atypical network with irregular distribution, closely resembling the reference 16 invasive melanoma imaged with the same device.

Facial-type lesion with pigmented follicular openings, asymmetric annular-granular pattern, blue-gray areas, irregular scalloped borders and obliterated follicles, which suggests lentigo maligna (melanoma).
Sun-damaged skin with a poorly defined, multifocal tan-olive pigmentation, irregular dark central dots and granules, and asymmetric pigment islands suggest lentigo maligna-type melanoma in situ.

Only part of the lesion is visible at the edge of the frame; that part shows a fairly regular brown reticular-to-globular pattern with a smooth, well-defined border and a slightly dark focal area, but no clear blue-white veil, atypical vessels or regression.

Small light-to-medium brown lesion with a fairly regular reticular/globular pattern, central hypopigmentation, and a mildly irregular lobulated border, but uniform color and no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels, favoring a dysplastic/junctional nevus.

Asymmetric lesion on sun-damaged freckled skin with a pink-red hypopigmented area containing dotted/irregular vessels adjacent to an irregular brown pigmented network, indicating multiple colors and structural asymmetry suggestive of hypomelanotic melanoma.

A large, poorly defined, faint tan-brown patchy lesion with irregular, discontinuous pigment islands and a fine vascular pattern on sun-damaged pink skin resembles the lentigo maligna–type in situ references.

Hypopigmented, ill-defined pink-tan macule with polymorphous dotted and short irregular red vessels, milky-red areas and scattered red globules on sun-damaged freckled skin, suggesting amelanotic/hypomelanotic melanoma.
Small, asymmetric, poorly defined lesion on sun-damaged background with eccentric dark brown blotch, irregular peppered/dotted granules and pinkish-red hue, resembling the reference melanoma 11.
Large asymmetric reddish-brown lesion with irregular globules/cobblestone areas, multiple white shiny streaks (chrysalis structures) and regression-like white areas, and an irregular border.

Small, ill-defined pinkish-brown to violaceous lesion with a homogeneous structureless center, a faint pigment network blending into freckled sun-damaged background skin, and no clear atypical network, streaks or regression structures, favoring a benign (possibly dermal) nevus, though the bluish-violet center leaves some concern.
Ulcerated, bleeding nodule with a blue-white veil, milky-red areas, polymorphous vessels and an eccentric black-blue blotch, all highly suspicious for nodular melanoma.

Large lesion filling the field with irregular, broken brown pigment network, asymmetric patchy distribution, regression-like whitish and pinkish areas, and irregular vessels, suggesting lentiginous or regressing melanoma on sun-damaged skin.

Small, fairly symmetric oval light-brown lesion with uniform color, a regular faint network/globular pattern, and a smooth fading border, without blue-white structures, atypical vessels, or regression; the purple marker lines are surgical ink, not a lesion feature.

A small (~5 mm), lobulated, trefoil-shaped reddish-brown lesion with a fairly uniform reticular network and globules, a slightly darker inferior rim, and no blue-white veil or atypical vessels, which together favor a benign nevus with mild asymmetry.
An asymmetric, irregularly outlined dark brown-black lesion with uneven blotchy pigment and radial streak-like projections at the edges, apparently on ridged (possibly acral) skin.

A fairly uniform light-to-mid brown lesion with a fine regular network, sharp borders, a single color and no blue-white veil, atypical vessels or irregular dots, though the mildly asymmetric elongated shape keeps some residual concern.

Large, asymmetric light-brown lesion with patchy, irregular network islands at the periphery, a broad central white scar-like regression area, and radial streak-like lines, together suggesting regression within a melanoma rather than a uniform nevus.
Asymmetric, irregularly shaped lesion with an eccentric dark blue-black blotch, blue-gray veil-like areas, white shiny streaks and uneven peripheral extensions, all partly obscured by dense hair.

Asymmetric bilobed outline with an irregular projection, but uniformly light-to-medium brown regular globular/cobblestone pattern in both lobes, without blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels, favoring a (possibly dysplastic) nevus.
Small, fairly symmetric oval brown lesion with mostly uniform pigmentation and only a tiny dark focal dot at one pole, on sun-damaged pink skin, favoring a benign nevus.

Large, markedly asymmetric lesion with irregular, multilobulated borders, several colors (dark brown, light brown, blue-gray), a blue-white veil-like area with regression, and an irregular, eccentric distribution of pigment.

Fairly symmetric brown lesion with a regular peripheral reticular network and a central raised pinkish-violet area with slight blue-gray, most consistent with a dermal/compound nevus, though the central blue-gray tone keeps melanoma in the differential.

Small (~5 mm), fairly symmetric oval brown lesion with a regular, fine reticular-globular pattern, uniform brown color with a slightly darker center, and a smooth, gradually fading border with no blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels.

The lesion is markedly asymmetric with an irregular, multilobed outline, a thickened and irregular brown network, clustered dark dots off-centre in the upper right, and pale regression-like areas, though the fairly regular network leaves a dysplastic nevus as a close alternative.
Large lesion on chronically sun-damaged skin with an atypical, irregular pigment network, multiple colors including dark brown-black areas, blue-gray zones, and asymmetric irregular pigmentation.

A small, light-brown, fairly symmetric lesion with a regular peripheral rim of brown globules (a growing-nevus pattern), with no blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels, though the sun-damaged, lentigo-studded background keeps some suspicion.

Large, ill-defined pink amelanotic lesion with milky-red areas, polymorphous dotted and linear vessels, white shiny streaks, and scattered irregular brown blotches at the periphery on sun-damaged skin, suggesting amelanotic/hypomelanotic melanoma.
Asymmetric reddish-brown lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors, peripheral radial streak-like projections, central bluish-white veil-like area, scattered red dots and scale.

Pink-red, largely amelanotic lesion with polymorphous dotted and linear irregular vessels, milky-red areas and white structureless zones on sun-damaged facial-type skin, with only faint peripheral brown pigmentation, suggesting amelanotic or hypomelanotic melanoma.

Large lesion with a central blue-white veil and regression-like whitish scar areas, peppering-like gray-blue dots, and irregular eccentric dark brown blotches at the periphery with multiple colors and asymmetry.
Small round, fairly symmetric lesion with a regular rim of peripheral brown globules (growing-nevus/Spitzoid pattern), though the central bluish-purple area with dark dots adds some concern.

Oval, fairly symmetric lesion with a pinkish-brown homogeneous center, milia-like dots, and regular peripheral brown globules/dots, consistent with a compound nevus; no atypical network, streaks, or regression structures.

Fairly symmetric light-brown lesion with a regular reticular network fading at the periphery and central hypopigmentation, consistent with a dysplastic or compound nevus; the blue-gray marks at the upper edge look like surgical marker ink, and there are no regression structures, irregular blotches or atypical vessels.

An asymmetric lesion with an irregular, notched border and a prominent, thickened pigment network with uneven holes, plus patchy structureless hypopigmented areas, makes this an atypical network pattern that cannot be confidently called a benign nevus.

Small, asymmetric, bilobed brown macule on sun-damaged hairy skin, with irregular notched borders, an eccentric darker hyperpigmented focus, uneven pigment distribution and faint pinkish regression-like areas, resembling the in situ melanomas on chronically sun-exposed skin among the references.

Faint, ill-defined light-brown macule on sun-damaged skin with irregular asymmetric pigment islands, a darker eccentric blotch, and fine vessels, resembling lentigo maligna or in-situ melanoma in the reference set (refs 6 and 14).

Soft, skin-colored, papillomatous lobulated (cobblestone/globular) surface with symmetric outline, minimal light-brown central pigment, and no atypical network, blue-white veil or atypical vessels, consistent with a dermal/papillomatous nevus.

Small oval brown lesion, about 4-5 mm, with fairly symmetric central darker brown-orange pigmentation fading evenly to the periphery and no clear atypical network, regression, or blue-white structures, resembling the benign Reference 13 from the same setting, though a faint grey focus keeps some suspicion.

A broad longitudinal melanonychia band on the nail plate, with heterogeneous brown-to-gray-black pigmentation, irregular lines of uneven width, blurred borders and dark granular areas, raises concern for nail-unit melanoma.

Large, ill-defined lesion on chronically sun-damaged skin with multiple shades of brown, irregular blotches, scattered dark dots and granules, scale, regression-like white-pink areas and a reddish zone, which suggests lentigo maligna or melanoma rather than a nevus.
Large asymmetric lesion with eccentric dark brown-black area, blue-gray/whitish veil-like zone centrally, irregular pigment distribution and multiple colors with uneven borders.

Asymmetric lesion with an eccentric, irregular dark blue-black blotch carrying blue-white veil-like areas, set within a broad irregular brown periphery of atypical globules and network with uneven, blurred borders.
Asymmetric irregular brown lesion with angulated, streak-like extensions at the periphery, central blue-gray granular peppering (regression), and an uneven pigment network.

Asymmetric, elongated two-part lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, blue-gray/purple) with eccentric blue-gray blotch and regression-like areas, on sun-damaged hairy skin.

Small (~5 mm), uniformly light-brown lesion with a fairly regular reticular/globular pattern, slightly irregular but not notched borders, and no blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels, favoring a benign nevus.

Irregular, asymmetric light-brown lesion with angulated, projecting borders, central regression-like whitish scar area, peripheral gray dots/granules and pinkish vascular tinge on sun-damaged skin, suggesting melanoma in situ.

Faint, ill-defined pink-tan macule with eccentric darker brown blotch, dotted vessels and pinkish erythema, irregular color distribution resembling the hypomelanotic in situ references; pen markings suggest the clinician flagged it.

Large, asymmetric lesion with an irregular, atypical pigment network, eccentric darker blotches, multifocal hypopigmented areas and an irregular, notched border, resembling the melanoma in reference 16.

Large, ill-defined light-brown macule extending beyond the field, with irregular asymmetric pigmentation, an atypical fragmented network, regression-like white/pink areas and dotted vessels on sun-damaged skin, suggests lentigo maligna/melanoma in situ.

A small, uniformly brown, bilobed lesion with fairly regular radial streaks around the edge (a starburst/Reed-nevus-like pattern), with no blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels; the irregular shape keeps the probability moderate.

Large asymmetric multicomponent lesion with several colors (tan, brown, pink, blue-gray), irregular peripheral blotches and dots, central regression with white scar-like areas and shiny white streaks, and blue-gray peppering.

Asymmetric lesion with an irregular, notched border, eccentric multifocal brown blotches, and a central pinkish regression-like area with dotted and short linear vessels; a dysplastic nevus with central hypopigmentation remains a real alternative.

Small asymmetric tan-brown macule with irregular, eccentric darker brown blotches and a blurred, fading edge, on sun-damaged skin with surrounding lentigines, raising concern for early melanoma in situ.

Asymmetric, irregularly shaped tan-brown macule with an eccentric darker blotch, a separate satellite-like extension and blurred borders, on chronically sun-damaged skin with surrounding lentigines, a pattern suggestive of lentigo maligna.

Asymmetric brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with an atypical, irregular peripheral network, a central blue-gray structureless area, and an eccentric dark blue-black dot with peppering, all suggesting regression and atypia.
An amelanotic pink papule with polymorphous dotted and serpentine vessels, no pigment network, and a milky-red background, which is worrying for amelanotic melanoma over a dermal nevus.

Small (~5 mm), irregular light-brown lesion on shaved, sun-damaged skin with asymmetric radial streak-like projections, an irregular notched outline, and central regression-like whitish/red area with dotted vessels.
Small asymmetric lesion with an eccentric blue-gray to purple area, a whitish veil-like overlay and irregular dark clods, surrounded by a faint, uneven brown periphery on sun-damaged skin.

Large asymmetric lesion with irregular notched borders, peripheral irregular dots/globules and pseudopods, multiple shades of dark brown to black, a central black blotch, and pinkish regression/blue-white areas.

Large, multifocal, irregular brown-gray pigmentation on sun-damaged facial skin with follicular openings, asymmetric perifollicular pigmentation, gray dots/annular-granular structures and regression, suggestive of lentigo maligna.
Asymmetric brown lesion with irregular, notched borders, multiple shades of brown, an atypical network and irregular dark dots, and a central blue-white/gray veil-like area all favor melanoma.
Small lesion on sun-damaged skin with an eccentric blue-gray/violaceous area showing peppering and dots, irregular brown periphery with an atypical network, and asymmetric color distribution.

Pink-red, largely amelanotic lesion with irregular asymmetric outline, dotted vessels, and a central slightly elevated pink focus on sun-damaged skin, with ink marking around it, suggesting hypomelanotic melanoma.

Asymmetric brown lesion with an eccentric blue-gray area of granular peppering, irregular scattered dots and globules, and uneven pigment distribution with blurred borders, suggesting regression and atypia.

Eccentric black blotch with peripheral pseudopods/streaks at one edge, within a larger asymmetric light-brown lesion with irregular dots, globules and a pinkish regression-like area, giving multiple colors and structural asymmetry.

Large, asymmetric light-brown macule with irregular, polycyclic, notched borders and patchy islands of pigment separated by hypopigmented, regression-like areas, on chronically sun-damaged skin with telangiectasia, which suggests lentigo maligna or melanoma in situ.

A poorly defined pink, largely amelanotic patch with a central erosion or ulcer, dotted and polymorphous red vessels and faint irregular brown remnants on sun-damaged skin, resembling the amelanotic melanoma references.

Fairly symmetric brown lesion with a regular border and a faint, uniform peripheral network; mild central hypopigmentation with subtle pinkish-gray areas raises some concern, but there are no clear atypical network, streaks or blue-white veil.

Large lesion extending beyond the field, with an abrupt transition from a reddish-brown globular/cobblestone area to a featureless black-brown zone, plus asymmetric pigment, irregular dark blotches and whitish structures.

Asymmetric, irregularly bordered brown lesion with an atypical, uneven pigment network, a central whitish regression-like area, clustered irregular dots and globules at the left edge, and separate peripheral pigmented islands.

Large, markedly asymmetric lesion with a central blue-white veil and blue-gray zones, irregular streaks and pseudopods at the periphery, scattered irregular dots and globules, multiple colors, and irregular regression-like areas.

Small, fairly symmetric brown lesion with a regular reticular/globular pattern, uniform brown colors, and no blue-white veil, atypical vessels, or regression structures, though the borders are slightly fragmented.
Large asymmetric lesion with an atypical, irregular, broadened pigment network, multiple eccentric dark blotches, focal blue-gray areas and irregular borders with multicomponent pattern.

Small (~5 mm), symmetric, round lesion with uniform reddish-brown color, regular fine globular/reticular pattern and smooth, evenly fading borders, without blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels.

Large lesion filling the frame with an irregular, broken atypical network, multiple colors (light-to-dark brown with blue-gray/violaceous blotches), scattered dark dots, regression-like white areas and asymmetric structure.

Small, ill-defined pinkish-red macule with irregular, asymmetric clusters of brown dots/globules and a pink erythematous background, closely resembling reference 10 (an invasive melanoma with a hypomelanotic, dotted pattern).

Asymmetric, irregularly bordered brown macule on chronically sun-damaged facial skin with eccentric darker areas, dots, and faint peripheral pigmentation around follicular openings suggestive of lentigo maligna.

Large, ill-defined, light-brown patch on chronically sun-damaged skin with an irregular, faded network, asymmetric pigmentation, gray dots, and polymorphous red vessels, suggesting lentigo maligna-type melanoma.

Small, fairly symmetric dark brown lesion with a regular pigment network fading at the periphery, a few central dots, and a uniform color without blue-white structures or atypical vessels, favoring a nevus.
Asymmetric lesion with an eccentric dark brown-black blotch, an irregular broken pigment network that thins out unevenly toward the periphery, and ill-defined irregular borders.
Asymmetric brown lesion with irregular dark radial streaks, peripheral dots and pseudopod-like projections, eccentric dark blotches, and central whitish regression-like areas.

Asymmetric brown lesion with a blurred, structureless center, irregular peripheral dark dots and globules, and gray-violet granular pigment at the lower-right edge; this multicomponent pattern is concerning but not conclusive, and a dysplastic nevus remains possible.

Pink, hypopigmented lesion with irregular, asymmetric brown-gray pigment remnants, polymorphous dotted and linear irregular vessels, and whitish areas on sun-damaged skin, suggesting a hypomelanotic melanoma.

Ill-defined, nearly amelanotic pink-orange patch on sun-damaged facial skin, with no organized pigment network, irregular linear vessels and subtle scale, which raises concern for amelanotic melanoma or lentigo maligna.
Large asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors including blue-gray and violaceous areas, irregular dots/globules, and regression-like blue-white veil zones.

Ill-defined, asymmetric brown macule on wrinkled, sun-damaged skin with uneven darker perifollicular, ring-like pigmentation around a lighter center, suggestive of early lentigo maligna rather than a simple nevus.

A large facial-type pigmented patch fills the field, with uneven brown pigment surrounding follicular openings, peppered gray-brown dots and partial annular-granular pattern, irregular blotches and linear vessels, which together suggest lentigo maligna.
Small brown lesion on erythematous background with clustered brown globules and blotches but fairly symmetric shape, no blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels, favoring a benign nevus.

Small, nearly amelanotic pink-orange macule with structureless pigment, fine irregular linear and dotted vessels, and a slightly asymmetric outline on sun-damaged skin, resembling the hypomelanotic melanoma references.

A small, ill-defined light-brown macule on sun-damaged skin with surrounding lentigines has an eccentric, irregular, star-shaped dark-brown central blotch and faint asymmetric peripheral pigmentation, which is concerning for early melanoma in situ, though the call is uncertain.

Asymmetric lesion with an eccentric brown pigmented upper half showing irregular darker areas and streak-like projections, plus a pink-red structureless lower half with dotted vessels and milky-red areas, giving multiple colors and an asymmetric structure.

Asymmetric, irregularly shaped flat lesion on sun-damaged skin. It has two colors, a tan-brown area next to a pink-red zone containing dotted vessels, with no organized pigment network, a pattern suggestive of early melanoma such as lentigo maligna.

Large, ill-defined light-brown patch on sun-damaged, likely facial skin, with prominent follicular openings, asymmetric darker grey-brown eccentric areas, irregular pigmentation and pink regression-like zones, suggesting lentigo maligna.

Elongated, fairly symmetric reddish-brown lesion with a regular faint network, mostly uniform color and a smoothly fading border, plus only minor darker irregular areas on the left without blue-white veil or atypical vessels, favoring a nevus.

Asymmetric reddish-brown lesion with irregular cobblestone globules, uneven peripheral dots and pseudopod-like projections concentrated at the lower edge, and focal central blue-gray areas, all suggesting an atypical pigment pattern.

Small, fairly symmetric brown lesion with a regular pigment network, mild central hypopigmentation, a few central dots and fading borders, and no blue-white veil or atypical vessels, consistent with a benign nevus.

Brown lesion with a fairly regular reticular-globular network that fades gradually at the periphery, with only mild asymmetry, a few darker eccentric patches and no regression or blue-white structures, favoring a dysplastic nevus over melanoma.
A hair-bearing scalp site with a pale pink, largely structureless area and only a single dark dot, outlined by surgical marker ink, without a visible atypical network, streaks or blue-white veil.

Uniformly light-brown, fairly symmetric lesion with a regular fine reticular network that fades at the periphery, no blue-white veil, regression or atypical dots, consistent with a junctional nevus, though the slightly irregular, fringed border keeps some uncertainty.

Large, highly asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (brown, dark brown, blue-gray), blue-white veil/regression structures, central pink-red scar-like area, irregular dots/globules and fragmented pigment network at the periphery.
Asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, eccentric dark brown-black irregular dots and globules, an atypical broken network and regression-like whitish areas on sun-damaged skin.

Irregular, asymmetric light-brown macule on sun-damaged skin with a broken, atypical network, central regression-like hypopigmented area, eccentric darker dots/streaks, and satellite-like separate pigmented islands, suggesting lentigo maligna/melanoma in situ.

Small, sharply demarcated brown lesion with an irregular bilobed shape but a fairly uniform, prominent pigment network and only two shades of brown, with no blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels, which favors a nevus.

A small asymmetric lesion with central erosion or crust, scattered dark dots, eccentric irregular brown pigment at the edge, and a surrounding pink-red halo; these features favor melanoma over a traumatized nevus, though that remains possible.
Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (brown, black, blue-gray), a blue-white veil, a white scar-like regression area, an irregular border and surface scale/crust.
Asymmetric irregular brown lesion on sun-damaged skin with blue-gray peppering/regression, eccentric pink-red vascular area extending from the pigment, and irregular extensions at the border.

A small, fairly symmetric round dark-brown lesion with radial streaming and peripheral dots, suggesting a starburst (Reed/Spitz-type) nevus, though the central blue-gray areas and irregular peripheral dots leave real concern for melanoma.

A light-brown lesion with a fairly regular, fine pigment network that fades evenly at the periphery, monochromatic tan color, and no blue-white veil, atypical dots or regression structures; the surrounding purple is skin-marker ink.

Fairly symmetric brown lesion with a regular pigment network that fades gradually at the periphery, a few slightly darker central blotches, and no blue-white veil, atypical vessels or regression structures, favoring a benign nevus.

Small, fairly round and symmetric dark brown-black lesion with uniform color, regular border, and an even peripheral rim of fine network/globules, consistent with a hyperpigmented nevus, though the very dark color keeps some concern.

Small, fairly symmetric oval lesion with homogeneous reddish-brown pigmentation, a slightly darker center and smooth regular borders, without atypical network, regression or blue-white structures; the purple pen marks and hair are artifacts.
Large asymmetric lesion with central pink-white regression-like area, dotted and polymorphous vessels, irregular peripheral brown pigmentation with irregular dots/globules and multiple colors.

Light-brown macule on sun-damaged skin with an irregular, scalloped border and a central pinkish regression-like area, plus asymmetric peripheral pigmentation and focal dark dots, suggesting lentigo maligna or melanoma in situ.
Large asymmetric lesion with irregular polycyclic borders, multiple brown shades, eccentric dark blotches, and whitish regression-like areas on sun-damaged, hairy skin of an older patient.

Large chaotic lesion with multiple colors (black, dark brown, red, blue-gray), irregular peripheral black dots/globules, blue-white veil, scale/crust and a red ulcerated/hemorrhagic area, plus an asymmetric border.

A small, asymmetric, irregular dark-brown lesion with angulated, zig-zag lines and uneven pigment on chronically sun-damaged ear skin of an older patient, a pattern suggestive of lentigo maligna (melanoma in situ).

Large, asymmetric lesion with irregular multifocal dark red-brown blotches, atypical broadened network, regression-like pinkish-white and bluish-purple areas, and irregular borders, similar in style to reference 16 (melanoma).

Asymmetric lesion with irregular borders, multiple colors (light brown, dark brown, red-brown, blue-gray/whitish central area), irregularly distributed dark dots/globules at the periphery, and a lighter eccentric extension on sun-damaged skin.

Two adjacent light-to-medium brown patches with fairly regular reticular network, uniform tan-brown color, no blue-white veil, atypical vessels or regression, and similar lesions nearby, all favoring benign nevi despite some asymmetry and a central hypopigmented area in the left patch.

Small (~4 mm), fairly symmetric oval brown lesion with a regular reticular pattern and a slightly darker eccentric center, without blue-white veil, atypical vessels, or irregular streaks; however, it sits on sun-damaged skin, which keeps the melanoma risk moderate.

Raised, sharply circumscribed nodule with blue-white veil-like structureless areas, an eccentric black-brown blotch, and scattered red dots and globules; this multicolor pattern is concerning for nodular melanoma despite the symmetric outline.
Large, asymmetric, multicomponent lesion with blue-white veil, dark black-purple irregular blotches, irregular dots/globules, regression-like white areas and multiple colors.

Very small, light-to-medium brown lesion with a slightly irregular, angulated outline but uniform color, no blue-white veil, no atypical network, and no vascular structures, most consistent with a small benign nevus.
Small, ill-defined light-brown macule on sun-damaged skin with irregular pigmentation, an eccentric darker reddish-brown area, and faint satellite patches, resembling the in situ melanoma references.

Irregular, asymmetric pigmented lesion on sun-damaged skin with eccentric dark brown-black irregular blotches and dots, angulated/rhomboidal structures around follicular openings, and an atypical, uneven pigment pattern suggestive of lentigo maligna-type melanoma.

Asymmetric reddish-brown lesion with irregular, notched border, an atypical network that varies in thickness, peripheral dots and globules, and white regression-like streaks and areas, resembling reference 16.
Asymmetric, lobulated outline with an eccentric satellite lobe, a pigment network that thickens irregularly toward the center, and central gray-violet darkening on a lesion about 8 mm across.

Facial lesion on sun-damaged skin with faint, ill-defined tan pigmentation around follicular openings, pinkish erythema, and fine irregular linear vessels, which suggests possible hypomelanotic lentigo maligna rather than a typical nevus.

Small but asymmetric lesion with irregular orange-brown and dark brown-black pigmentation, eccentric blue-gray dots/globules, and a bluish veil-like area at the lower edge, suggesting melanoma despite its small size.

Small, ill-defined pinkish-red macule with dotted/irregular vessels and faint irregular brown pigmentation on sun-damaged skin full of solar lentigines, resembling the hypopigmented/amelanotic melanoma references.

Irregular, asymmetric light-brown macule on sun-damaged facial skin (vellus hairs, telangiectasias) with uneven pigmentation, annular-granular/perifollicular pattern and ill-defined borders, suggestive of lentigo maligna.

A small (~4 mm), fairly symmetric brown lesion with a central darker zone, a faint network fading at the periphery and overlying scale, but no blue-white veil, atypical vessels or irregular streaks, favoring a nevus.

Small (~3 mm), light-brown lesion with a fairly regular, symmetric reticular network that fades at the periphery, with no blue-white veil, atypical dots, or regression, favoring a benign junctional nevus; the parallel streak-like extensions at the edges (likely skin-fold/acral-type pattern) are the main reason for some residual concern.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (dark brown, black, blue-gray, pink-red), irregular dots and globules at the periphery, a blue-white veil, regression structures, and a milky-red area with atypical vessels.
Small asymmetric lesion with an orange-brown crusted portion and an eccentric dark blue-black/gray area, giving multiple colors and blue-gray structures that raise concern despite its small size.

Large asymmetric lesion with multiple colors (brown, blue-black, pink-red), blue-white veil areas, peripheral irregular brown blotches, central pink regression/milky-red area with polymorphous vessels.

Asymmetric, irregularly shaped darker brown patch with an atypical, broadened and unevenly distributed pigment network and blotches on a background of sun-damaged skin with diffuse lentiginous pigmentation.

Large, amelanotic pink-red lesion with ulcerated/crusted areas, white structureless and scale-like zones, dark crust at the edge and polymorphous red areas, suggesting an invasive amelanotic melanoma.

Large (>15 mm), irregular, poorly demarcated light-brown macule on sun-damaged skin with an atypical patchy network, regression-like pink areas with dotted/linear vessels, and multifocal asymmetric pigmentation, suggestive of melanoma in situ or lentigo maligna type.

Asymmetric dark lesion with blue-white veil, irregular dark-brown/black globules and blotches, and satellite-like peripheral clods detached from the main body, giving multiple colors and an irregular structure.

Large lesion filling the frame with multifocal irregular brown blotches, an atypical network, extensive white regression-like structureless areas, peppering and gray-blue dots, and asymmetric patchy pigment distribution, all favoring melanoma (likely on sun-damaged skin).

Cobblestone and globular pattern in the main papillomatous lesion and in the clustered satellite components, with curved comma-like vessels and no atypical network, streaks or blue-white veil, suggest a congenital/dermal nevus; the whitish areas are the main residual concern.

Asymmetric lesion with central pink-white regression and pinkish vascular blush, eccentric irregular dark-brown blotches and clods at the periphery, and irregular pigment distribution on sun-damaged skin.

Asymmetric lesion with an eccentric dark violaceous-brown area showing blue-gray peppering, whitish regression-like zones, irregular globules/dots and a heterogeneous network, raising concern despite fairly regular borders.
A largely amelanotic pink lesion with irregular, polymorphous vessels, white shiny structureless areas and surface scale, and no regular pigment network, which raises concern for amelanotic melanoma.

Small, fairly symmetric reddish-brown lesion with a regular fine pigment network, uniform color with slight central hyperpigmentation, and smooth well-defined borders without regression, blue-white veil, or atypical vessels, consistent with a benign nevus.

Small, fairly symmetric oval lesion of uniform tan-brown colour with a regular globular/reticular pattern and a slightly fringed but even periphery, without blue-white veil, regression or atypical vessels, favouring a benign nevus.

Large, highly asymmetric lesion with irregular lobulated borders, multiple colors (dark brown-black, tan, pink, blue-gray), a central blue-white veil with regression structures, and peripheral dark blotches and irregular dots.

Pinkish-red, largely hypopigmented lesion on sun-damaged, hairy skin with a faint, irregular brown network at the periphery, dotted vessels and poorly defined borders, suggestive of hypomelanotic melanoma similar to references 8 and 10.

Sun-damaged background with an ill-defined, multifocal tan-brown lesion showing irregular dark eccentric blotch, angulated/rhomboidal structures and asymmetric pigmented islands with pink vascular areas, suggestive of lentigo maligna.
Large lesion filling the field with an irregular outline, uneven brown-gray pigment, an atypical broken network, regression-like white structureless areas, and peripheral gray dots and blotches.

Small but asymmetric lesion with irregular, notched borders, eccentric darker area, blue-gray structures, and a whitish reticular (negative network-like) pattern centrally, raising concern despite its small size.

Small, symmetric, round lesion with uniform homogeneous tan-brown color and a regular rim of peripheral dots/globules, suggesting a growing but symmetric nevus, with no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical network.

Large, markedly asymmetric lesion with two distinct zones: a dark reddish-brown part on one side and a lighter pink-tan part on the other with an irregular, fragmented network, plus multiple colors and regression-like areas.

Ill-defined, asymmetric central brown-gray macule on sun-damaged skin with solar lentigines, showing irregular dots/globules, gray granular areas and an atypical network, which suggests lentigo maligna or melanoma in situ.

Small (~5 mm), fairly round and symmetric brown lesion with uniform globular/granular pattern and a regular border, showing only slight central darker grayish area and no atypical network, streaks, or regression structures.

Large lesion extending beyond the field of view, with an atypical irregular network, multiple colors (brown, black, pink, blue-gray), irregular dark blotches and dots, regression-like gray-pink areas, and an asymmetric, irregular border.

A light tan, fairly symmetric oval lesion with a regular fine network and milia-like dots, and only a single eccentric darker brown focus of network and globules at the upper right, which favors a benign (likely dysplastic) nevus over melanoma.

Small, fairly symmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with a regular network and globules, a uniform color palette and no regression, blue-white veil or atypical vessels; a few peripheral dots are only a minor concern.

Ill-defined, faint pink-tan macule on sun-damaged skin with polymorphous dotted/linear irregular vessels, pinkish structureless areas and asymmetric, patchy light-brown pigmentation, a pattern suggestive of hypomelanotic or amelanotic melanoma.
Large asymmetric lesion with multiple browns and dark blue-black blotches, irregular broken pigment network with eccentric dark areas, regression-like whitish zones and polymorphous linear vessels.

Uniform light-brown lesion with a regular fine pigment network and evenly spaced follicular openings, smooth fading borders, and no blue-white veil, atypical vessels or regression structures, similar to the benign Reference 1.

Large, hairy, fairly symmetric light-to-medium brown lesion with a regular, uniform reticular network that fades gradually at the periphery, and no blue-white veil, atypical vessels, or irregular dots, favoring a benign (possibly congenital-pattern) nevus.

Irregular, asymmetric light-brown lesion with multifocal patchy pigmentation, an eccentric darker area with atypical broadened network, and blurred, irregular borders on sun-damaged skin, suggestive of lentigo maligna/melanoma in situ.
Large asymmetric multicomponent lesion with a dark blue-black blotch, peripheral radial streaming, central white regression scar, irregular scattered brown-orange patches and multiple colors.
A large, asymmetric dark-brown lesion with an irregular, notched border, uneven pigment density (a darker upper portion and a lighter, structureless lower area) and blurred network at the periphery.

A small (about 5 mm), fairly uniform light-to-mid brown lesion with a regular reticular network and no blue-white structures, dots or atypical vessels favours a nevus, though the jagged outline with peripheral network projections on sun-damaged skin keeps some concern.

Largely amelanotic pink lesion with polymorphous, irregular dotted, glomerular and serpentine vessels, milky-red areas, and peripheral irregular dark brown-gray streaks and dots, raising strong concern for amelanotic or hypomelanotic melanoma.
Faint, ill-defined light-brown macule on sun-damaged skin with irregular dots/globules, fine linear/dotted vessels and pinkish hue, resembling the early in situ/hypomelanotic melanoma references.
The lesion is asymmetric, with several eccentric dark blotches and irregular radial streaks (pseudopods) confined to one side, while the opposite side is featureless, light brown and blurred.
Small (~2 mm), symmetric oval brown lesion with a darker central hyperpigmented spot and a regular faded periphery, single color, no regression structures or atypical vessels.

Lesion on sun-damaged skin with surrounding lentigines, showing irregular asymmetric pigmentation, a central blue-gray/purple area, eccentric dark dots and globules, and an atypical irregular network, a pattern favoring melanoma (likely in situ).

A sharply demarcated, round, symmetric papillomatous lesion with many whitish milia-like clods set in a uniform reddish-brown background, with no atypical network, streaks or blue-white veil, fits a seborrheic keratosis or papillomatous nevus.
Large asymmetric lesion with irregular notched borders, uneven brown pigmentation and eccentric blue-gray dots/peppering suggesting regression within an atypical network.

Large, ill-defined, multifocal lesion with irregular reddish-brown globules and dots, pink areas with polymorphous vessels, and blue-white structureless regression areas, suggesting regressing or invasive melanoma.

Large, asymmetric lesion with irregular jagged borders and protrusions, multiple shades of brown with gray-blue granular/peppered areas, irregular dots and globules, and an atypical network on sun-damaged skin.

Fairly symmetric oval brown lesion with a regular, uniform pigment network and globular/cobblestone-like pattern, sharp smooth borders, and no blue-white veil, regression, or atypical vessels, all favoring a benign nevus.
Small, light-brown, fairly uniform lesion on hair-bearing scalp skin with a faint regular reticular-globular pattern, no blue-white veil, atypical vessels, or dark asymmetric areas.

The lesion is small (about 3 mm) and dark brown-black with a fairly well-defined, if notched, outline and fairly uniform pigment, though the irregular shape and dark central blotch on sun-damaged skin keep melanoma a real possibility.

Large lesion with a predominantly brown reticular network, multifocal patchy hyperpigmented islands, and a network that thins and fades at the periphery; there is no blue-white veil and no atypical vessels, favoring a dysplastic or Clark nevus, though the asymmetry keeps some concern.

Large (~10 mm) lesion with multiple asymmetric colors (brown, dark brown, blue-gray area), irregular eccentric dark blotches, a central pinkish regression-like zone, and a blue-white veil-like region.

Uniform light-brown, regular reticular pigment network with central hypopigmentation, symmetric oval shape, single color, and gradual fading at the periphery, without blue-white structures, atypical dots or vessels.

A small, nearly featureless pink-tan macule on sun-damaged skin with dotted vessels, few white dots and almost no pigment network; it resembles the hypomelanotic melanomas in the references, though its symmetry and small size make a benign lesion nearly as likely.

Fairly symmetric oval lesion with a regular peripheral brown reticular network fading at the edges and a central pinkish hypopigmented area, which fits a dysplastic or compound nevus, though the eccentric darker foci and scattered dots keep moderate suspicion.

Pink-red, largely amelanotic lesion with irregular shape, central whitish scar-like areas, dotted/polymorphous vessels and asymmetric peripheral brown remnants, which are concerning for hypomelanotic melanoma.

Small (~4 mm), fairly symmetric oval lesion with a regular brown network fading at the periphery and a small darker central area, without blue-white veil, atypical vessels or irregular streaks, consistent with a benign nevus.

The lesion is asymmetric and multicomponent, with an irregular outline, an atypical broadened network, and irregularly distributed brown and gray dots and globules (peppering) concentrated off-center, on sun-damaged background skin.

Small dark brown-black lesion with irregular, angulated borders, peripheral irregular projections, uneven pigment with central reddish-brown structureless area, on sun-damaged skin with surrounding solar lentigines.
Asymmetric, irregularly notched lesion with an atypical brown network, a central purplish blue-gray structureless area suggesting regression or veil, multiple colors, and surface scale.
Ill-defined, asymmetric pigmented macule on sun-damaged skin with an eccentric dark red-brown blotch, irregular brown granules/peppering, regression-like white areas, and atypical vessels.
Large lesion filling the field with irregular gray-blue to dark brown pigmentation, a central pinkish regression-like area with blue-white veil, peppering, and asymmetric multicomponent structure.

A large asymmetric lesion with an eccentric dark-brown atypical, thickened network in the upper right, irregular brown blotches, and pale structureless, regression-like areas with uneven pigment distribution.
A pink, amelanotic, poorly defined lesion with dotted and irregular linear vessels and no pigment network, resembling the pink invasive melanoma in Reference 8.

Asymmetric light-brown lesion with an irregular, broadened pigment network, several separate darker hyperpigmented areas, and irregularly scattered dark dots centrally, giving a disordered multicomponent pattern; the light colour and absence of regression or blue-white structures make a dysplastic nevus a real possibility.
